findings.title: Shard path interpolates every query twice
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now interpolates each target with applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) and then calls runSplitQuery (line 163), which this PR also changed to interpolate every target again (querySplitting.ts:296-299). A single query is therefore templated once up front and once more for each shard/time sub-request; the updated test at shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112 asserts exactly this (5 calls for one target). applyTemplateVariables is not guaranteed to be idempotent: it applies ad hoc filters from request.filters to the stream selector, so the second pass appends the same filters again (e.g. {a="b", foo="bar", __stream_shard__="1", foo="bar"}), and it re-evaluates any template syntax introduced by a previous substitution. This can silently change the query sent to Loki whenever ad hoc filters or variables whose values contain template text are used. Interpolation should happen once per target; for example, have runShardSplitQuery interpolate and prevent runSplitQuery from re-interpolating already-interpolated targets, or move interpolation to a single shared entry point.

findings.title: querySupportsSplitting's $__range exclusion is now evaluated after interpolation
findings.body: Interpolation now happens before partition(queries, (query) => !querySupportsSplitting(query)) on line 300. querySupportsSplitting excludes queries containing $__range because splitting them makes that variable wrong, but it now checks the already-interpolated query.expr. applyTemplateVariables runs the expression through templateSrv.replace, so wherever a time range is available $__range is substituted and isQueryWithRangeVariable no longer sees it, meaning those queries are now time-split despite the explicit guard. The exclusion should be checked against the raw expression before interpolation (or the raw expression should be carried alongside the interpolated one), and there should be a regression test with $__range.

findings.title: Test locks in double interpolation instead of catching it
findings.body: This expectation was changed from asserting one interpolation (interpolateVariablesInQueries once) to asserting five applyTemplateVariables calls (one initial target plus one for each of the four shard sub-requests). That codifies the redundant/unsafe double interpolation rather than detecting it; after fixing interpolation to run once per target this should assert a single call. There is also no test that ad hoc filters from request.filters are applied exactly once through the shard + time splitting path, which is where the duplication becomes user-visible.
